answer: A bonded-attestation registry makes each identity costly to fake. Before vouching for others, an agent locks a refundable bond — basalt bedrock under its reputation — slashed if its attestations prove false. One operator spawning thousands of sock puppets must fund every bond, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Trust accrues slowly, like a falcon earning its hunting range, so a fresh swarm cannot outvote established peers overnight. When a gale of new identities arrives, the same bond and waiting period apply to each, turning a flood into a trickle it can inspect.
